probably best if we set the config's default push mode to 'manual'

## Current state

`project.pushMode` defaults to `auto` in both `CONFIG_ENTRIES` and `DEFAULT_PROJECT_CONFIG`. The config service uses the first value when a project config is missing or omits `pushMode`; project-folder creation uses the second. Explicit saved values already override these defaults.

Auto mode pushes after persistence operations. Manual mode keeps commits pending, reports the pending state, and exposes the explicit Push action.

## Implementation details

- Change both push-mode defaults from `auto` to `manual`.
- Keep explicit `auto` and `manual` values unchanged. Add no migration or compatibility branch; configs without `pushMode` receive the new default.
- Do not change push execution, pending-commit restoration, persistence notifications, or Push action visibility.
- Update config-service and project-creation tests that assert the default.

## Acceptance criteria

- New projects persist `pushMode: "manual"`.
- Missing project config, or project config without `pushMode`, resolves to manual mode.
- Explicit `pushMode: "auto"` still enables automatic pushes; explicit manual mode keeps current behavior.
- Tests cover both default paths and explicit-value preservation.

# Architectural decisions

Project-wide decisions for MDÂ². The app is a Vite React web app in `app/`; `desktop/` is a separate Electron host that can load the website and expose local capabilities through preload bridges.

## File naming

| Decision | Rule | Rationale |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Code files use lowercase snake_case names. | All code files in `app/src/` and `desktop/` use lowercase words separated by underscores, for example `github_auth_service.ts`, `project_workspace.tsx`, and `local_git_service.js`. Test files keep the same base name with `.test` before the extension, for example `github_auth_service.test.ts`. Exported symbols keep normal TypeScript/JavaScript casing such as `GithubAuthService`, `ProjectWorkspace`, and `useGithubAuth`. | A single file naming convention avoids mixed PascalCase, camelCase, and hyphenated filenames, and keeps imports predictable across Windows and case-sensitive environments. |

## Services and state

| Decision | Rule | Rationale |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Global singleton services own domain state and logic. | Each domain is a class in `src/services/**`, instantiated once at module level and exported, for example `export const indexesService = new IndexesService()`. React components do not own domain state. | Keeps business logic out of components, testable without a DOM, and shared across windows/views without Redux, Zustand, or Context stores. |
| Service location follows usage scope. | If a service is specific to one UI element and used only there, place it beside that component. Generic or shared services, such as logging, database access, config, storage, or cross-screen domain logic, belong in `src/services/`. | Keeps component-owned behavior local while preserving `src/services/` for reusable application services. |
| Consumers use direct imports or the service injector. | Direct import when no import cycle exists; use `src/services/service_injector.js` when a cycle would occur. Every global singleton service registers itself in its constructor with `inj.register('myService', this)`. | The service graph is dense; the injector is a bare global registry that defers resolution to call time. |
| Services have a two-phase lifecycle. | Constructors only register and set unloaded state such as `null`. Config-dependent or service-dependent work runs in `init()`, `start()`, app bootstrap (`App.jsx`), or a `loaded` lifecycle event. `configService.config` is private; callers use `get`, `set`, and `clear`. | Module evaluation order is not guaranteed, so `configService` is not usable at import time. Reading config in a constructor is a bug. |


## Events and React integration

| Decision | Rule | Rationale |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Services notify observers through their own `EventTarget`. | Services expose an `EventTarget` and dispatch named `CustomEvent` domain events such as `activeIndex`, `added`, `deleted`, or `changedBox`. Observers subscribe with `addEventListener` and unsubscribe with `removeEventListener` on the owning service. | Decouples producers from consumers without depending on Node `EventEmitter`, which is not available in the browser-first React app. |
| Custom hooks bridge service events to functional components. | Hooks in `src/components/hooks/`, such as `useActiveIndex` and `useProjectConfig`, seed `useState` from a service property, subscribe in `useEffect`, unsubscribe in cleanup, and return the value. Prefer hook + service over prop chains. | Components stay declarative and avoid direct event plumbing. |
| Components subscribe at the smallest rendering boundary. | Root and layout components compose UI regions and pass structural inputs. Components that render changing application data subscribe through hooks themselves. Do not hoist changing data into ancestors only to pass it downward. | Limits rerenders to affected UI, protects transient state such as open popups, and avoids broad prop chains. |
| Components use the app theme service path. | `App` owns theme mode through `useThemeMode()`, builds the MUI theme with `createAppTheme(mode)`, and provides it through `ThemeProvider`. Components read theme values with MUI APIs such as `useTheme`, `useMediaQuery`, and `sx`; only controls that change the palette mode receive `mode` and `onToggleTheme`. | Theme state, persistence, and palette construction stay centralized while components remain presentation-focused. |

| Code files use lowercase snake_case names. | All code files in `app/src/` and `desktop/` use lowercase words separated by underscores, for example `github_auth_service.ts`, `project_workspace.tsx`, and `local_git_service.js`. Test files keep the same base name with `.test` before the extension, for example `github_auth_service.test.ts`. Exported symbols keep normal TypeScript/JavaScript casing such as `GithubAuthService`, `ProjectWorkspace`, and `useGithubAuth`. | A single file naming convention avoids mixed PascalCase, camelCase, and hyphenated filenames, and keeps imports predictable across Windows and case-sensitive environments. |

## Services and state

| Decision | Rule | Rationale |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Global singleton services own domain state and logic. | Each domain is a class in `src/services/**`, instantiated once at module level and exported, for example `export const indexesService = new IndexesService()`. React components do not own domain state. | Keeps business logic out of components, testable without a DOM, and shared across windows/views without Redux, Zustand, or Context stores. |
| Service location follows usage scope. | If a service is specific to one UI element and used only there, place it beside that component. Generic or shared services, such as logging, database access, config, storage, or cross-screen domain logic, belong in `src/services/`. | Keeps component-owned behavior local while preserving `src/services/` for reusable application services. |
| Consumers use direct imports or the service injector. | Direct import when no import cycle exists; use `src/services/service_injector.js` when a cycle would occur. Every global singleton service registers itself in its constructor with `inj.register('myService', this)`. | The service graph is dense; the injector is a bare global registry that defers resolution to call time. |
| Services have a two-phase lifecycle. | Constructors only register and set unloaded state such as `null`. Config-dependent or service-dependent work runs in `init()`, `start()`, app bootstrap (`App.jsx`), or a `loaded` lifecycle event. `configService.config` is private; callers use `get`, `set`, and `clear`. | Module evaluation order is not guaranteed, so `configService` is not usable at import time. Reading config in a constructor is a bug. |


## Events and React integration

| Decision | Rule | Rationale |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Services notify observers through their own `EventTarget`. | Services expose an `EventTarget` and dispatch named `CustomEvent` domain events such as `activeIndex`, `added`, `deleted`, or `changedBox`. Observers subscribe with `addEventListener` and unsubscribe with `removeEventListener` on the owning service. | Decouples producers from consumers without depending on Node `EventEmitter`, which is not available in the browser-first React app. |
| Custom hooks bridge service events to functional components. | Hooks in `src/components/hooks/`, such as `useActiveIndex` and `useProjectConfig`, seed `useState` from a service property, subscribe in `useEffect`, unsubscribe in cleanup, and return the value. Prefer hook + service over prop chains. | Components stay declarative and avoid direct event plumbing. |
| Components subscribe at the smallest rendering boundary. | Root and layout components compose UI regions and pass structural inputs. Components that render changing application data subscribe through hooks themselves. Do not hoist changing data into ancestors only to pass it downward. | Limits rerenders to affected UI, protects transient state such as open popups, and avoids broad prop chains. |
| Components use the app theme service path. | `App` owns theme mode through `useThemeMode()`, builds the MUI theme with `createAppTheme(mode)`, and provides it through `ThemeProvider`. Components read theme values with MUI APIs such as `useTheme`, `useMediaQuery`, and `sx`; only controls that change the palette mode receive `mode` and `onToggleTheme`. | Theme state, persistence, and palette construction stay centralized while components remain presentation-focused. |

Code already supports Claude multi-turn streaming, resume, questions, tool logs, file tracking, and usage. Gap: Claude tool approvals auto-denied; reasoning and rich tool lifecycle lack Codex parity.

Should F_134 target:

1. Full parity: approvals, reasoning, tool lifecycle, diagnostics.
2. Only existing multi-turn streaming behavior.
codex --model gpt-5.6-sol -c model_reasoning_effort=medium --sandbox workspace-write --ask-for-approval on-request app-server --stdio
Scope fixed: full Claude parity. Inspect approval UI/data flow plus official Claude control protocol before edit.
title: add support for request approval

`CodexStreamingAdapter` handles structured questions, but not Codex app-server approval requests. `item/fileChange/requestApproval` and `item/commandExecution/requestApproval` fall through as protocol diagnostics, for example `item/fileChange/requestApproval: unknown (...)`. No approval UI or JSON-RPC response exists, so the turn remains blocked.

- Handle both approval methods as server-initiated JSON-RPC requests before notification handling. Validate request, item, thread, and turn ids; track pending requests by request id; clear them on `serverRequest/resolved`.

- Add a dedicated approval contract through `AgentRunnerService`, action execution events, Electron preload/local bridge, and remote control. Respond with `{ decision }`; for command requests, honor `availableDecisions` when supplied. Keep approvals separate from structured questions and conversation messages.

- Store pending approvals in `ActionExecutionService`. Keep execution `waitingForInput` while any question or approval remains. Replay must restore unresolved approvals and discard resolved ones after renderer reload.

- Add a separate popup approval component. Show reason plus command, working directory, parsed actions, network host/protocol, requested permissions, or affected file paths when available. Actions sit bottom-right: allow once, allow for session, decline, and stop turn. Show policy-amendment choices only when Codex supplies them.
- Support multiple pending approvals without overwriting one another. Disable a submitted request until response or resolution; reject duplicate, stale, mismatched, or unsupported decisions clearly.
- Do not persist approval requests or decisions in conversation/activity files or agent handoff context. Existing completed command/file activity remains authoritative.
- Add adapter, runner, execution-contract, bridge, remote-control, service, popup, reload, and regression tests. Run lint and tests in `desktop/` and `app/`.
- File-change and command-execution approval requests show actionable prompts instead of protocol diagnostics.
- Allow once/session, decline, stop-turn, and offered policy-amendment choices send the exact matching JSON-RPC decision and unblock Codex.
- Approval UI shows available security context before user decides, including network-specific context when present.
- Concurrent requests remain isolated; `serverRequest/resolved`, turn completion, or cancellation removes only matching pending requests.
- Renderer reload and remote-control clients retain correct pending approval state.
- Structured questions, activity ordering, changed-path tracking, and conversation persistence keep existing behavior; approval data is not persisted.

entries.content: Findings complete. Claude has basic long-lived stream, but lacks token deltas, reasoning/tool lifecycle, and approvals. Existing approval contract Codex-shaped; design must make it provider-neutral while preserving Codex behavior.

---
author: 
id: F_134
internalId: b9792dd7-f034-4b29-9da5-04fc8cea37c9
title: add support streaming claude
status: design
owner: 
affects:
agents:
  - design/activity/card__b9792dd7-f034-4b29-9da5-04fc8cea37c9.json#conversation=agent-ed0e1ddd-ff8c-4d8b-8073-ca17195697fa
policy:
after: 
---

Currently, we only have full support for streaming agents for the codex agent. we should do the same for the claude agent

## Current state

Claude actions already run as a persistent `stream-json` process with multi-turn messages, session resume, structured questions, file-change tracking, tool transcripts, usage, and terminal-state handling. However, assistant output arrives only as completed messages; thinking and detailed tool lifecycle events are ignored. Every non-question `can_use_tool` request is denied because the approval contract and UI are Codex-specific.

## Implementation details

- Enable Claude partial messages and normalize text, thinking, tool-use, tool-result, and diagnostic events into the existing conversation-entry lifecycle. Use stable provider item ids, preserve provider order, and replace streamed state with authoritative completion without duplicate output.
- Convert non-question Claude `can_use_tool` requests into provider-neutral approvals. Show tool name, input, reason, paths/command, and provider permission suggestions when supplied. Map allow once/session, decline, and stop-turn to exact Claude `control_response` payloads; keep `AskUserQuestion` on the question path.
- Refactor approval types, runner events, bridges, run registry, and popup only as needed to support both Claude and Codex shapes. Preserve concurrent-request, submitted/resolved, reload, and remote-control behavior.
- Keep Claude session resume/fallback, queued messages, usage, changed-path tracking, persistence, and Codex streaming behavior unchanged. Add adapter, runner, bridge, registry, popup, and regression tests in `desktop/` and `app/`.

## Acceptance criteria

- Claude assistant text, thinking, and tool activity update during a turn, remain ordered, and contain no duplicates after completion.
- Claude permission requests show actionable security context; each offered decision sends the matching control response and unblocks or stops the turn.
- Structured questions remain separate from approvals; multiple pending interactions remain isolated and survive renderer reload.
- New and resumed Claude conversations support multiple turns, missing-session fallback, usage, file tracking, queued messages, and terminal states.
- Codex streaming and approval behavior remains unchanged; automated tests cover both providers.

Currently, we only have full support for streaming agents for the codex agent. we should do the same for the claude agent

## Current state

Claude actions already run as a persistent `stream-json` process with multi-turn messages, session resume, structured questions, file-change tracking, tool transcripts, usage, and terminal-state handling. However, assistant output arrives only as completed messages; thinking and detailed tool lifecycle events are ignored. Every non-question `can_use_tool` request is denied because the approval contract and UI are Codex-specific.

## Implementation details

- Enable Claude partial messages and normalize text, thinking, tool-use, tool-result, and diagnostic events into the existing conversation-entry lifecycle. Use stable provider item ids, preserve provider order, and replace streamed state with authoritative completion without duplicate output.
- Convert non-question Claude `can_use_tool` requests into provider-neutral approvals. Show tool name, input, reason, paths/command, and provider permission suggestions when supplied. Map allow once/session, decline, and stop-turn to exact Claude `control_response` payloads; keep `AskUserQuestion` on the question path.
- Refactor approval types, runner events, bridges, run registry, and popup only as needed to support both Claude and Codex shapes. Preserve concurrent-request, submitted/resolved, reload, and remote-control behavior.
- Keep Claude session resume/fallback, queued messages, usage, changed-path tracking, persistence, and Codex streaming behavior unchanged. Add adapter, runner, bridge, registry, popup, and regression tests in `desktop/` and `app/`.

## Acceptance criteria

- Claude assistant text, thinking, and tool activity update during a turn, remain ordered, and contain no duplicates after completion.
- Claude permission requests show actionable security context; each offered decision sends the matching control response and unblocks or stops the turn.
- Structured questions remain separate from approvals; multiple pending interactions remain isolated and survive renderer reload.
- New and resumed Claude conversations support multiple turns, missing-session fallback, usage, file tracking, queued messages, and terminal states.
- Codex streaming and approval behavior remains unchanged; automated tests cover both providers.

# Architectural decisions

Project-wide decisions for MDÂ². The app is a Vite React web app in `app/`; `desktop/` is a separate Electron host that can load the website and expose local capabilities through preload bridges.

## File naming

| Decision | Rule | Rationale |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Code files use lowercase snake_case names. | All code files in `app/src/` and `desktop/` use lowercase words separated by underscores, for example `github_auth_service.ts`, `project_workspace.tsx`, and `local_git_service.js`. Test files keep the same base name with `.test` before the extension, for example `github_auth_service.test.ts`. Exported symbols keep normal TypeScript/JavaScript casing such as `GithubAuthService`, `ProjectWorkspace`, and `useGithubAuth`. | A single file naming convention avoids mixed PascalCase, camelCase, and hyphenated filenames, and keeps imports predictable across Windows and case-sensitive environments. |

## Services and state

| Decision | Rule | Rationale |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Global singleton services own domain state and logic. | Each domain is a class in `src/services/**`, instantiated once at module level and exported, for example `export const indexesService = new IndexesService()`. React components do not own domain state. | Keeps business logic out of components, testable without a DOM, and shared across windows/views without Redux, Zustand, or Context stores. |
| Service location follows usage scope. | If a service is specific to one UI element and used only there, place it beside that component. Generic or shared services, such as logging, database access, config, storage, or cross-screen domain logic, belong in `src/services/`. | Keeps component-owned behavior local while preserving `src/services/` for reusable application services. |
| Consumers use direct imports or the service injector. | Direct import when no import cycle exists; use `src/services/service_injector.js` when a cycle would occur. Every global singleton service registers itself in its constructor with `inj.register('myService', this)`. | The service graph is dense; the injector is a bare global registry that defers resolution to call time. |
| Services have a two-phase lifecycle. | Constructors only register and set unloaded state such as `null`. Config-dependent or service-dependent work runs in `init()`, `start()`, app bootstrap (`App.jsx`), or a `loaded` lifecycle event. `configService.config` is private; callers use `get`, `set`, and `clear`. | Module evaluation order is not guaranteed, so `configService` is not usable at import time. Reading config in a constructor is a bug. |


## Events and React integration

| Decision | Rule | Rationale |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Services notify observers through their own `EventTarget`. | Services expose an `EventTarget` and dispatch named `CustomEvent` domain events such as `activeIndex`, `added`, `deleted`, or `changedBox`. Observers subscribe with `addEventListener` and unsubscribe with `removeEventListener` on the owning service. | Decouples producers from consumers without depending on Node `EventEmitter`, which is not available in the browser-first React app. |
| Custom hooks bridge service events to functional components. | Hooks in `src/components/hooks/`, such as `useActiveIndex` and `useProjectConfig`, seed `useState` from a service property, subscribe in `useEffect`, unsubscribe in cleanup, and return the value. Prefer hook + service over prop chains. | Components stay declarative and avoid direct event plumbing. |
| Components subscribe at the smallest rendering boundary. | Root and layout components compose UI regions and pass structural inputs. Components that render changing application data subscribe through hooks themselves. Do not hoist changing data into ancestors only to pass it downward. | Limits rerenders to affected UI, protects transient state such as open popups, and avoids broad prop chains. |
| Components use the app theme service path. | `App` owns theme mode through `useThemeMode()`, builds the MUI theme with `createAppTheme(mode)`, and provides it through `ThemeProvider`. Components read theme values with MUI APIs such as `useTheme`, `useMediaQuery`, and `sx`; only controls that change the palette mode receive `mode` and `onToggleTheme`. | Theme state, persistence, and palette construction stay centralized while components remain presentation-focused. |

    sequence?: number

    agent: string
    conversationId: string
    createdAt: string
    lastUsedAt: string

}

    content: string

    durationMs?: number
    exitCode?: number
    id: string
    label?: string
    output?: string
    providerItemId?: string
    sequence?: number
    status?: string
    summary?: string[]
    timestamp: string

}

    kind: 'event'

    workingFolder: string

design\releases\0_0_3\F_76_action_streaming_or_oneshot_agent_mode.md:23:Multi-turn today is **faked**: each turn is a new process, continuity comes from `buildResumeAgentCommand` (`claude --resume <id>` / `codex exec resume --json <id>`) plus transcript replay through `contextInput`. design\activity\project.json:170:          "content": "\n===== B_80_worktree_selector_not_updated.md =====\r\n---\r\nauthor: \r\nid: B_80\r\ninternalId: e69b9faf-30dd-4ad6-9d99-7e6af4d18c76\r\ntitle: worktree selector not updated\r\nstatus: ready\r\nowner: \r\naffects:\r\nagents:\r\n  - design/activity/card__e69b9faf-30dd-4ad6-9d99-7e6af4d18c76.json#conversation=agent-e533433a-31ad-4168-8a1c-f57869151ddd\r\npolicy:\r\nafter: \r\n---\r\nafter the 'integrate into project' command is run on a card that is assigned to a worktree, the worktree selector icon is not updated and the wrong state is shown on the card. if the user clicks again on the icon and runs the 'integrate into project' again, the app gives an error to say nothing left to integrate. then the icon gets updated correctly\r\n\r\n## Current state\r\n\r\n`WorktreeSelector` derives its arrows and enabled actions from records published by `WorktreeService`. Integration creates a squash commit on the project branch, but leaves the linked branch on its original commits. Git therefore still reports the worktree as ahead and behind. A second integration rebases away those already-integrated commits, publishes the corrected state, then fails because nothing remains to integrate.\r\n\r\nCard integration also commits its activity record after the integration refresh, so that new project commit is absent from the published status.\r\n\r\n## implementation details\r\n\r\n- After a successful squash, move the clean linked branch to the integration commit before publishing worktree state. Keep its assignment and branch; do not park or unassign it.\r\n- After card activity persistence completes, synchronize the linked branch to the new project head and publish worktree state again.\r\n- Keep project-level integration on the shared synchronization path; it needs no activity refresh.\r\n- Preserve existing integration and activity-persistence errors. If post-integration synchronization fails, report the partial failure and keep the card assigned.\r\n- Add desktop Git and bridge regression tests. Existing renderer subscription should update without component-local state.\r\n\r\n## acceptance criteria\r\n\r\n- Successful integration immediately removes the outgoing indicator and disables `Integrate into project`.\r\n- Card integration finishes with no outgoing or incoming indicator and disables both integration and update actions.\r\n- Reopening the selector or waiting for polling is unnecessary.\r\n- A second integration is not required to correct the icon and is unavailable when no outgoing changes remain.\r\n- Card and project integrations publish correct final worktree status; failure behavior remains unchanged.\r\n\n===== B_81_new_card_markdown_typing_lag.md =====\r\n---\r\nauthor:\r\nid: B_81\r\ninternalId: 8e4a295a-8788-4232-8be7-c97f5a1cf5c8\r\ntitle: new card Markdown typing lag\r\nstatus: ready\r\nowner:\r\naffects:\r\nagents:\r\npolicy:\r\nafter: ff356504-eed4-47f3-bb38-2c749b6fcba6\r\n---\r\n\r\n## Problem\r\n\r\nTyping in the **New card** description editor has noticeable input lag.\r\n\r\nPerformance trace `Trace-20260731T140458.json` records five input events that each block the renderer main thread for 52-64 ms. Layout and paint are small; synchronous React work consumes most of the time.\r\n\r\n## Cause\r\n\r\n`NewCardDialog` passes `handleBodyChange` to `MarkdownEditor.onLiveChange`. Every editor change calls `setBody`, rerendering the complete dialog and the MDXEditor subtree. This also recreates the Markdown editor plugin array and many MUI elements and style objects. Development-mode React work and garbage collection amplify the cost.\r\n\r\nThis bypasses the lifetime-stable editor approach already used by `CardEditor` and `CardBodyEditor`. `MarkdownEditor` already buffers local edits and exposes `getMarkdown`, `setMarkdown`, and `flush`; normal typing does not need to propagate the full body into parent React state.\r\n\r\n## Required change\r\n\r\n- Keep the new-card Markdown editor lifetime-stable while typing, following `CardEditor` and `CardBodyEditor`.\r\n- Do not store the full Markdown body in `NewCardDialog` state on every keystroke.\r\n- Read the current body from the editor when submitting, checking whether the draft is dirty, and inserting or clearing the template.\r\n- Preserve existing template behavior: untouched template can be cleared; editing it changes the action back to `Template`; inserting then appends without discarding text.\r\n- Keep reset, cancel confirmation, `Ctrl+Enter`, and target-column behavior unchanged.\r\n- Do not change shared `MarkdownEditor` buffering semantics solely for this dialog.\r\n\r\n## Acceptance criteria\r\n\r\n- [ ] Typing in the new-card description does not rerender `NewCardDialog` or remount/rerender the Markdown editor for every keystroke.\r\n- [ ] Submitted card body exactly matches current editor content.\r\n- [ ] Cancel confirmation detects description-only edits.\r\n- [ ] Template insert, clear, edit, and append behavior remains unchanged.\r\n- [ ] Opening, closing, successful creation, and project changes reset the draft correctly.\r\n- [ ] A regression test verifies repeated description edits do not repeatedly render the editor boundary.\r\n- [ ] Existing new-card dialog and Markdown editor tests pass.\r\n\n===== B_82_orphaned_git_for_windows_processes.md =====\r\n---\r\nauthor:\r\nid: B_82\r\ninternalId: d97a054f-5a67-47bb-9070-df874cf9148e\r\ntitle: agent runs leave orphaned Git for Windows processes\r\nstatus: ready\r\nowner:\r\naffects:\r\nagents:\r\npolicy:\r\nafter: 7bdf27fc-963c-4545-83e2-93410e67f0e3\r\n---\r\n\r\n## Problem\r\n\r\nAgent runs launched through MDÃ‚Â² can leave multiple `git.exe` processes running indefinitely. The processes appear as **Git for Windows** in Task Manager and accumulate across runs.\r\n\r\nObserved processes were executing normally short-lived commands such as `config`, `rev-parse`, `remote -v`, and `status --porcelain`. They remained alive after their immediate parent processes had exited.\r\n\r\n## Current implementation\r\n\r\nMDÃ‚Â² starts agents through `AgentRunnerService`. When an agent closes normally, `handleClose` queries the current Windows process tree and terminates descendants of the agent PID. Cancellation terminates the process tree with `taskkill /t /f`.\r\n\r\nThis cleanup cannot discover a surviving Git process after an intermediate parent has already exited: the current process snapshot no longer contains a complete chain from the agent PID to that Git process. The observed Git processes had dead immediate parents, matching this failure mode.\r\n\r\nMDÃ‚Â² also invokes Git directly through `git_commands.js`. These calls have no timeout or cancellation handling, so an independently hung app-owned Git command can block its caller indefinitely.\r\n\r\n## Investigation plan\r\n\r\n1. Reproduce with MDÃ‚Â² open but no agent run, then while starting and completing or cancelling an agent run.\r\n2. Record every spawned Git PID, command, working directory, parent PID, agent run ID, and lifecycle event.\r\n3. Run an affected command under a bounded external timeout with Git tracing enabled to locate the blocking operation.\r\n4. Check repository state, Git configuration, filesystem monitoring, antivirus or file locks, and agent shutdown ordering.\r\n5. Confirm whether Git descendants become disconnected before `AgentRunnerService.handleClose` takes its process snapshot.\r\n\r\n## Required change\r\n\r\n- Track enough process ownership during an agent run to terminate surviving descendants even when intermediate processes exit before final cleanup.\r\n- Clean up owned descendants when an agent completes, fails, is cancelled, or crashes.\r\n- Do not terminate unrelated Git processes or Git work started outside the corresponding MDÃ‚Â² agent run.\r\n- Add a bounded timeout and process cleanup to direct Git execution in `git_commands.js`.\r\n- Include the command, working directory, elapsed time, and owning run or app operation in timeout diagnostics.\r\n- Deduplicate or serialize repeated read-only metadata probes only if tracing confirms they contribute to the accumulation.\r\n\r\n## Failure modes and compatibility\r\n\r\n- PID reuse must not allow cleanup to target a process that MDÃ‚Â² did not start.\r\n- Cleanup must cover shell and helper-process chains used by Git for Windows on Windows.\r\n- Long-running network Git operations need an explicit, suitable timeout rather than the same threshold as local metadata commands.\r\n- Existing agent cancellation, command actions, commits, worktree operations, push, pull, and fetch behavior must remain unchanged apart from bounded failure and cleanup.\r\n\r\n## Acceptance criteria\r\n\r\n- [ ] Completing, failing, cancelling, or crashing an agent run leaves no Git processes owned by that run.\r\n- [ ] Repeated agent runs do not accumulate Git for Windows processes.\r\n\n===== B_85_add_the_reference_to_a_chatlog_to_a_card_as_soon_as_possible.md =====\r\n---\r\nauthor: \r\nid: B_85\r\ninternalId: 56dd54b0-9554-4545-85d4-bb45efef4d6e\r\ntitle: add the reference to a chatlog to a card as soon as possible\r\nstatus: ready\r\nowner: \r\naffects:\r\nagents:\r\n  - After history is selected, `handleConversationChange` only loads persisted paths, so popup cannot return to empty conversation state.\r\n\r\n# Implementation details\r\n\r\n- Keep empty `Conversations` item selectable while picker is enabled.\r\n- Treat empty value as reset: clear selected conversation and displayed chat without calling conversation loader.\r\n- Next run omits `continueFrom` and starts new conversation.\r\n\r\n# Acceptance criteria\r\n\r\n- User can select `Conversations` after selecting historical conversation.\r\n- Popup returns to empty conversation without error or empty-path load.\r\n- Next run starts new conversation; selecting history still continues selected conversation.\r\n- Picker and controller tests cover reset and continuation behavior.\r\n\n===== F_115_add_support_for_request_approval.md =====\r\n---\r\nauthor: \r\nid: F_115\r\ninternalId: 7bdf27fc-963c-4545-83e2-93410e67f0e3\r\ntitle: add support for request approval\r\nstatus: ready\r\nowner: \r\naffects:\r\nagents:\r\npolicy:\r\nafter: 56dd54b0-9554-4545-85d4-bb45efef4d6e\r\n---\r\n# Current state\r\n\r\n`CodexStreamingAdapter` handles structured questions, but not Codex app-server approval requests. `item/fileChange/requestApproval` and `item/commandExecution/requestApproval` fall through as protocol diagnostics, for example `item/fileChange/requestApproval: unknown (...)`. No approval UI or JSON-RPC response exists, so the turn remains blocked.\r\n\r\n# Implementation details\r\n\r\n- Handle both approval methods as server-initiated JSON-RPC requests before notification handling. Validate request, item, thread, and turn ids; track pending requests by request id; clear them on `serverRequest/resolved`.\r\n- Add a dedicated approval contract through `AgentRunnerService`, action execution events, Electron preload/local bridge, and remote control. Respond with `{ decision }`; for command requests, honor `availableDecisions` when supplied. Keep approvals separate from structured questions and conversation messages.\r\n- Store pending approvals in `ActionExecutionService`. Keep execution `waitingForInput` while any question or approval remains. Replay must restore unresolved approvals and discard resolved ones after renderer reload.\r\n- Add a separate popup approval component. Show reason plus command, working directory, parsed actions, network host/protocol, requested permissions, or affected file paths when available. Actions sit bottom-right: allow once, allow for session, decline, and stop turn. Show policy-amendment choices only when Codex supplies them.\r\n- Support multiple pending approvals without overwriting one another. Disable a submitted request until response or resolution; reject duplicate, stale, mismatched, or unsupported decisions clearly.\r\n- Do not persist approval requests or decisions in conversation/activity files or agent handoff context. Existing completed command/file activity remains authoritative.\r\n- Add adapter, runner, execution-contract, bridge, remote-control, service, popup, reload, and regression tests. Run lint and tests in `desktop/` and `app/`.\r\n\r\n# Acceptance criteria\r\n\r\n- File-change and command-execution approval requests show actionable prompts instead of protocol diagnostics.\r\n- Allow once/session, decline, stop-turn, and offered policy-amendment choices send the exact matching JSON-RPC decision and unblock Codex.\r\n- Approval UI shows available security context before user decides, including network-specific context when present.\r\n- Concurrent requests remain isolated; `serverRequest/resolved`, turn completion, or cancellation removes only matching pending requests.\r\n- Renderer reload and remote-control clients retain correct pending approval state.\r\n- Structured questions, activity ordering, changed-path tracking, and conversation persistence keep existing behavior; approval data is not persisted.\r\n\n===== F_89_add_support_for_clicking_on_links_in_chatlogs.md =====\r\n---\r\nauthor: \r\nid: F_89\r\ninternalId: 9ef42f8e-d6f7-4514-8e4a-5555318c4b51\r\ntitle: add support for clicking on links in chatlogs\r\nstatus: ready\r\nowner: \r\naffects:\r\nagents:\r\npolicy:\r\nafter: e69b9faf-30dd-4ad6-9d99-7e6af4d18c76\r\n---\r\nSometimes the agent produces a link to a local project file. Normalize separators and convert paths inside the active repository to repository-relative paths.\r\n- When the target is inside configured `projectFolder` and is either a Markdown file or a loaded action-definition JSON file, switch to list view and open its existing Markdown or action editor.\r\n- Open every other local project file in VS Code through the Electron bridge. Windows links to Markdown files under configured `projectFolder` opens them in list view with the Markdown editor.\r\n- Clicking relative or absolute Windows links to action-definition JSON files under configured `projectFolder` opens them in list view with the action editor.\r\n- Clicking another local project-file link opens that file in VS Code.\r\n- Invalid, missing, or out-of-project file links show an error and leave app usable.\r\n- Tests cover path normalization, internal editor routing, VS Code fallback, and error handling.\r\n\n===== F_90_redesign_add_new_card_dialog.md =====\r\n---\r\nauthor: \r\nid: F_90\r\ninternalId: eb3a4820-0edb-4161-8fe5-926a981d2c8f\r\ntitle: redesign add new card dialog\r\nstatus: ready\r\nowner: \r\naffects:\r\nagents:\r\npolicy:\r\nafter: d97a054f-5a67-47bb-9070-df874cf9148e\r\n---\r\nReference mockup: `New Card Dialog.dc.html` (desktop + mobile side by side, light/dark toggle top-right).\r\nStyle tokens and component conventions: bold headings, so it dominates the dialog, doesn't look editable, and must be deleted for most cards.\r\n* Title Ã¢â‚¬â€ the one field that always matters Ã¢â‚¬â€ is visually secondary.\r\n* Type is a dropdown, which costs two clicks for a short, known list.\r\n* The footer's \"Adds to \\<column>\" is static text, so the target column can't be changed without closing the dialog.\r\n* Net result: lots of empty space, little usefulness.\r\n\r\n## Scope\r\n\r\nTwo presentations of the same form and the same state:\r\n\r\n* **Desktop** Ã¢â‚¬â€ centered modal dialog over a scrim.\r\n* **Mobile** Never hard-code hex values per type; if a type has no color, fall back to a neutral token (`--text-4`).\r\n* Selected state: tinted background + border in the app's primary token, primary text color. Unselected: subtle track background, secondary text, transparent border; hover raises contrast.\r\n* Default selection: the app's existing default type (first in the list if there is no configured default).\r\n* Overflow: desktop wraps to multiple lines; mobile scrolls horizontally in one row (no wrap, no visible scrollbar chrome).\r\n* Keyboard: arrow keys move between pills, Space/Enter selects; the row is a single tab stop (radiogroup semantics Ã¢â‚¬â€ `role=\"radiogroup\"` with `role=\"radio\"` + `aria-checked` children).\r\n\r\n\n===== F_91_remove_finished_reasoning_blocks.md =====\r\n---\r\nauthor: \r\nid: F_91\r\ninternalId: 3ffa4da3-1e0f-4930-ad38-6bf247b13c52\r\ntitle: remove finished reasoning blocks\r\nstatus: ready\r\nowner: \r\naffects:\r\nagents:\r\npolicy:\r\nafter: eb3a4820-0edb-4161-8fe5-926a981d2c8f\r\n---\r\n\r\nwhen a reasoning output of an agent finishes, we should remove the block\r\n\r\n## Current state\r\n\r\nCodex reasoning is stored as an `AgentConversationEvent`. Streaming updates replace the same event by `providerItemId`, changing its status from `inProgress` to `completed`. `ActionConversationChat` currently renders every reasoning event, so completed reasoning blocks remain visible during the live run and in reopened conversations. Failed and declined reasoning already use the error presentation.\r\n\r\n## implementation details\r\n\r\n- Filter conversation feed activities in `ActionConversationChat`: omit only events where `type === 'reasoning'` and `status === 'completed'`.\r\n- Keep in-progress, failed, declined and unknown-status reasoning visible.\r\n- Keep completed reasoning events in conversation data and persisted history; this is a presentation-only change.\r\n- Update chat tests for live completion, reopened conversations, failed/declined reasoning and unaffected non-reasoning activities.\r\n\r\n## acceptance criteria\r\n\r\n- In-progress reasoning is visible.\r\n- A reasoning block disappears when its status becomes `completed`, including after reopening a conversation.\r\n- Failed and declined reasoning remains visible with its error state and content.\r\n- Completed non-reasoning activities remain visible.\r\n\n===== F_94_no_prefill_prompt_running_conv.md =====\r\n---\r\nauthor: \r\nid: F_94\r\ninternalId: d4afff38-5581-42f4-a8f3-8ded807ab27a\r\ntitle: no prefill prompt running conv\r\nstatus: ready\r\nowner: \r\naffects:\r\nagents:\r\npolicy:\r\nafter: 3ffa4da3-1e0f-4930-ad38-6bf247b13c52\r\n---\r\n\r\nWhen an agent is waiting for a response, but the action popup was closed or on the wrong 'action', then when the user clicks on the action to view the conversation and answer, the input box is prefilled again with the action's prompt. this is annoying cause it needs to be removed.\r\n\r\nso, when activating an action that has a running conversation, don't prefill the input\r\n\r\n# Current state\r\n\r\n`useActionPopupController` prepares an action's stored prompt for a new conversation. When popup opens on another action, or reopens while execution state is being restored, that prepared prompt can remain in `promptState` when user selects action with a `queued`, `running`, or `waitingForInput` conversation.\r\n\r\n# Implementation details\r\n\r\n- Give active execution its own prompt identity, including before active-child metadata arrives.\r\n- When active action is selected, seed editor only from its shared user-entered draft; otherwise show empty input.\r\n- Invalidate pending prompt preparation and bump `promptResetToken` when action becomes active.\r\n- Keep stored-prompt prefill for idle actions starting new conversations. Keep command actions unchanged.\r\n\r\n# Acceptance criteria\r\n\r\n- Selecting or reopening action with active conversation does not prefill its stored action prompt.\r\n- Existing user-entered draft for active conversation is restored.\r\n- Late prompt-preparation result cannot overwrite active conversation input.\r\n- Idle agent actions still prefill stored prompt.\r\n- Controller and popup tests cover action switching, popup reopen, draft restore, and preparation race.\r\n\n===== F_95_integrate_into_project_should_track_commit.md =====\r\n---\r\nauthor: \r\nid: F_95\r\ninternalId: e5b95f2c-cd0c-4623-8e12-d0c497447e71\r\ntitle: integrate into project should track commit\r\nstatus: ready\r\nowner: \r\naffects:\r\nagents:\r\n  - design/activity/card__e5b95f2c-cd0c-4623-8e12-d0c497447e71.json#conversation=agent-4e6f97b9-647e-49fc-93f7-cf09e5eff1aa\r\npolicy:\r\nafter: 9ef42f8e-d6f7-4514-8e4a-5555318c4b51\r\n---\r\n\r\n## Current state\r\n\r\n`WorktreeSelector` integrates an assigned card through `WorktreeService` and the Electron worktree service. The backend checkpoints primary-worktree changes, rebases the card branch when behind, then fast-forwards the project branch. The operation returns no commit metadata.\r\n\r\nCard commit history reads tracked `<projectFolder>/activity/card__<cardInternalId>.json` files. Only action executions add commit references, so commits integrated from the selector are absent unless an action already recorded them.\r\n\r\n## Implementation details\r\n\r\n- Add a card-specific integration request containing `cardInternalId` and `projectFolder`; project-level worktree integration remains untracked.\r\n- After any rebase, squash the card branch's complete change onto the project branch and create one integration commit. Do not fast-forward or retain the card branch's individual commits on the project branch.\r\n- Resolve the integration commit's activity metadata, then append one system activity record containing only that commit and labeled `Integrate into project` to the card's primary-checkout activity file. Do not model it as a user action.\r\n- Commit the activity-file update through the existing serialized activity writer. Return only after both integration and history persistence finish, so existing card-history reload and diff UI show the integration commit.\r\n- If applying or committing the squash fails, restore the primary checkout to its state after the primary-worktree checkpoint and before the squash attempt.\r\n- Failed integration writes no activity record. If integration succeeds but activity persistence fails, report that partial failure clearly; never claim tracking succeeded.\r\n\r\n## Acceptance criteria\r\n\r\n- Integrating a card worktree with one or several outgoing commits creates and records exactly one squash commit under the card's stable `internalId`.\r\n- The squash commit contains the combined change between the project branch and the rebased card branch. Primary checkpoint and activity-file commits are not included.\r\n- The squash commit appears once under `Integrate into project` in the existing card commit selector and opens one combined diff for the integration.\r\n- Integration with no outgoing commits or no combined change remains rejected and creates no activity record.\r\n- Failed integration creates no activity record. History-persistence failure after a successful squash commit is visible.\r\n- Project-level worktree integration creates no card activity.\r\n- Tests cover one and several source commits producing one squash commit, rebase before integration, stable card ownership, squash cleanup and persistence failure paths, and project-level exclusion.\r\n\n===== F_96_ctrl_enter_on_action_input.md =====\r\n---\r\nauthor: \r\nid: F_96\r\ninternalId: d33002d3-ee0e-4c08-8e26-36f790500ee2\r\ntitle: ctrl enter on action input\r\nstatus: ready\r\nowner: \r\naffects:\r\nagents:\r\npolicy:\r\nafter: d4afff38-5581-42f4-a8f3-8ded807ab27a\r\n---\r\n\r\nwhen pressing ctrl + enter on action input, the input is sent, this is good, but before this happens, the input box still adds an enter, which should not be the case.\r\n\r\n# Current state\r\n\r\n`ActionAgentPrompt` handles `Ctrl+Enter` and `Meta+Enter` on the prompt wrapper during event bubbling. MDXEditor handles `Enter` first, inserts a newline, then the wrapper flushes and sends the changed prompt.\r\n\r\n# Implementation details\r\n\r\n- Intercept `Ctrl+Enter` and `Meta+Enter` during capture, before MDXEditor handles the key.\r\n- Prevent default behavior and stop propagation, then flush the latest prompt before running the existing shortcut callback.\r\n- Keep plain `Enter`, `Shift+Enter`, and disabled shortcut behavior unchanged.\r\n- Extend `action_agent_prompt.test.tsx` with regression coverage proving the editor does not receive the send shortcut.\r\n\r\n# Acceptance criteria\r\n\r\n- `Ctrl+Enter` sends current prompt without inserting a newline.\r\n- `Meta+Enter` has same behavior.\r\n- Prompt is flushed before send callback runs.\r\n- Plain `Enter` and `Shift+Enter` still insert newlines.\r\n\n===== F_98_worktree_vs_project_folder_placeholders.md =====\r\n---\r\nauthor: \r\nid: F_98\r\ninternalId: ff356504-eed4-47f3-bb38-2c749b6fcba6\r\ntitle: worktree vs project folder placeholders\r\nstatus: ready\r\nowner: \r\naffects:\r\nagents:\r\npolicy:\r\nafter: d33002d3-ee0e-4c08-8e26-36f790500ee2\r\n---\r\nWe have 'rootProjectFolder' placeholder. this currently maps to the folder that the agent is running on, so it could the the main project folder or a worktree. \r\n\r\nWe need to improve this and split it up in `worktree-folder` and 'project-folder' where the last one always references the main project folder while 'worktree-folder' references the folder that the agent is currently running in.\r\n\r\nAlso, we need to add the 'releases-folder' as well\r\n\r\n## Current state\r\n\r\n- `{{rootProjectFolder}}` exists in action prompt/command and diff-command placeholder sets.\r\n- Action execution resolves it to the execution checkout, which may be the opened project folder or a linked worktree. Diff commands resolve it to the opened project folder.\r\n- Action editor insertion controls and user documentation expose only the existing placeholder.\r\n\r\n## implementation details\r\n\r\n- Replace `{{rootProjectFolder}}` everywhere with `{{worktree-folder}}` and `{{project-folder}}`; do not keep a legacy alias.\r\n- `{{worktree-folder}}` resolves to the absolute execution checkout path. When no linked worktree is selected, it equals `{{project-folder}}`.\r\n- `{{project-folder}}` always resolves to the absolute opened repository path, including during linked-worktree execution.\r\n- Add `{{releases-folder}}`, resolving to the configured repository-relative releases path: `<projectFolder>/<releasesFolder>`.\r\n- Support all three placeholders in action prompts, action commands, prompt preparation, diff commands, editor insertion controls, validation, and documentation.\r\n- Fail before process start when a required placeholder value is unavailable. Add tests for primary and linked-worktree execution, custom release paths, diff commands, insertion controls, and removed `{{rootProjectFolder}}` support.\r\n\r\n## acceptance criteria\r\n\r\n- Primary-checkout actions resolve `{{worktree-folder}}` and `{{project-folder}}` to the opened repository path.\r\n- Linked-worktree actions resolve `{{worktree-folder}}` to that worktree and `{{project-folder}}` to the opened repository path.\r\n- `{{releases-folder}}` returns the configured path relative to repository root, independent of active checkout.\r\n- Action prompts, action commands, and diff commands use the same three folder placeholders.\r\n- Editors and documentation list the new placeholders and no longer list `{{rootProjectFolder}}`.\r\n- `{{rootProjectFolder}}` is not resolved.\r\n\n===== J_020_unify_agent_conversation_entries.md =====\r\n---\r\nauthor:\r\nid: J-020\r\ninternalId: 4edefccb-f7e3-4ae1-9c0d-5939ac1d3745\r\ntitle: unify agent conversation messages and events into ordered entries\r\nstatus: ready\r\nowner:\r\naffects:\r\n  - shared/agent_conversations.mjs\r\n  - desktop/src/actions/agent/agent_conversation.js\r\n  - desktop/src/actions/agent/agent_runner_service.js\r\n  - desktop/src/actions/agent/agent_transcript.js\r\n  - app/src/data/data_types.ts\r\n  - app/src/data/action_run_types.ts\r\n  - app/src/services/actions/action_execution_service.ts\r\n  - app/src/services/agents/card_agent_state.ts\r\n  - app/src/components/actions/use_action_popup_controller.ts\r\n  - app/src/components/actions/action_conversation_chat.tsx\r\npolicy:\r\n  checkLinting: true\r\n  requireTests: true\r\nafter: c5d963f2-ca43-419d-bc3c-972199b7e7cd\r\n---\r\n\r\n## Goal\r\n\r\nReplace the parallel agent-conversation `messages` and `events` arrays with one canonical ordered `entries` array. Array position is ingestion order and is the only display order.\r\n\r\nThis refactor must land before the action-popup rendering-isolation work. That work must consume the single entry list and must not preserve the current merge-and-sort path.\r\n\r\n## Terminology\r\n\r\n- **Conversation entry**: one ordered item in an agent conversation.\r\n- **Message entry**: user or assistant text.\r\n- **Event entry**: reasoning, tool use, command execution, diagnostics, failures, and lifecycle observations.\r\n\r\nDo not use **activity** for a conversation entry, field, helper, component, or collection. `activity` remains valid only for the separate card/project activity-storage domain.\r\n\r\n## Current architecture\r\n\r\nPersisted `AgentConversation` stores `messages` and `events` separately. Live execution repeats the split as `LiveAgentTurn.messages` and `LiveAgentTurn.activities`. Producers append or replace items in those separate collections, while chat and transcript consumers merge and sort them by `sequence` to reconstruct ingestion order.\r\n\r\nThe split causes:\r\n\r\n- duplicate persisted and live representations;\r\n- inconsistent `event`/`activity` terminology;\r\n- repeated merge and sort work in consumers;\r\n- a rebuilt full `AgentConversation` projection in the popup controller;\r\n- ordering behavior owned by presentation code instead of the producer.\r\n\r\n## Required model\r\n\r\nUse a discriminated union and one collection:\r\n\r\n```ts\r\n\n===== J_021_derive_markdown_styles_globally.md =====\r\n---\r\nauthor:\r\nid: J-021\r\ninternalId: 11ffc4ac-44e0-4dab-a8d9-af9e83a43aff\r\ntitle: derive active Markdown content styles once in the global theme\r\nstatus: ready\r\nowner:\r\naffects:\r\n  - app/src/theme/theme_context.ts\r\n  - app/src/theme/theme_provider.tsx\r\n  - app/src/theme/theme_provider.test.tsx\r\n  - app/src/theme/use_app_theme.ts\r\n  - app/src/components/editor/markdown_style_sx.ts\r\n  - app/src/components/editor/markdown_editor.tsx\r\n  - app/src/components/actions/action_conversation_chat.tsx\r\n  - app/src/components/config/markdown_style_preview.tsx\r\npolicy:\r\n  checkLinting: true\r\n  requireTests: true\r\nafter: 4edefccb-f7e3-4ae1-9c0d-5939ac1d3745\r\n---\r\n\r\n## Goal\r\n\r\nBuild the active Markdown content styling once when the global Markdown style configuration changes. links show an error and leave app usable.\r\n- Tests cover path normalization, internal editor routing, VS Code fallback, and error handling.\r\n\n===== F_90_redesign_add_new_card_dialog.md =====\r\n---\r\nauthor: \r\nid: F_90\r\ninternalId: eb3a4820-0edb-4161-8fe5-926a981d2c8f\r\ntitle: redesign add new card dialog\r\nstatus: ready\r\nowner: \r\naffects:\r\nagents:\r\npolicy:\r\nafter: a dropdown, which costs two clicks for a short, known list.\r\n* The footer's \"Adds to \\<column>\" is static text, so the target column can't be changed without closing the dialog.\r\n* Net result: lots of empty space, little usefulness.\r\n\r\n## Scope\r\n\r\nTwo presentations of the same form and the same state:\r\n\r\n* **Desktop** Ã¢â‚¬â€ centered modal dialog over a scrim.\r\n* **Mobile**
